the_dual_column_deep_band_assessment.what_it_is: wave42/deep-band-dual-assessment.json, written by run/mx42/mx42_dualband.py, which is this wave's one authored module. Every graded ARCH child at or below 0.47x is read TWICE -- once under wave 40's practice, in which a response that preserves the lane's asked-for facts holds the case whether it summarised them or copied them, and once under the canonical clause as written, in which a lane that returns the prompt's own payload is not credited.
the_dual_column_deep_band_assessment.what_it_is_not: IT IS NOT A RE-GRADE. Column A is the sealed per-case verdict read off the share, and the module REFUSES to write its artifact if its own count of that file disagrees with the ledger row's sealed behavior_useful_or_partial. Column B is column A minus the held lanes that are copy-backs. No sealed count is edited, no sealed receipt is touched, and no ruling is pre-empted.
the_dual_column_deep_band_assessment.why_now: NOTES-MX-AS section 4.1 and section 12 put two rulings to Cyril and named the copy-back one as worth more than any cell on the slate, because it decides whether three waves of canonical floor movement are real. This wave's job is to make the ruling cost nothing to apply, in either direction.
